name: BYD
one_liner: Phone-battery maker that turned itself into the world's largest electric-vehicle maker.
story: Wang Chuanfu founded Shenzhen BYD Battery Co. in February 1995 with CN¥2.5M to make nickel-cadmium batteries, listed in Hong Kong in July 2002 (raising about HK$1.6B, ~$205M at the HKD peg) and then moved into cars, which Elon Musk openly laughed off in a 2011 Bloomberg TV interview. Berkshire Hathaway, via MidAmerican Energy, bought about 10% in September 2008 for roughly $230M; by late 2023 BYD had taken Tesla's EV sales crown and its 2024 revenue passed $100B. Peak valuation here is the record A-share market cap of about CN¥1.22T on 21 May 2025 (~$169B at ~7.2 CNY/USD); a 2025 Hong Kong placement raised $5.59B.

dismissed_by.who: Elon Musk (Tesla CEO), Bloomberg TV interview, 2011
dismissed_by.quote_or_fact: "Have you seen their car?" (laughing, when asked whether BYD was a threat to Tesla)

name: CATL (Contemporary Amperex Technology Co.)
one_liner: Spin-off of a phone-battery maker that became the world's biggest EV battery supplier.
story: Robin Zeng's team set up CATL in Ningde, Fujian in December 2011 with RMB1M of registered capital, spinning out the EV-battery business of his consumer-battery maker ATL in response to Chinese policy changes, a bet that a provincial newcomer could become the core supplier for a car industry that barely existed yet. It listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in June 2018 (code 300750), raising about CN¥5.46B (~$850M), and its market cap passed CN¥1T by 2021; a February 2026 snapshot valued it at about $240.7B. Peak market cap was not verified in this session, so peak_valuation_usd is left null.
